# Appendix A. Single-modality derivations {#sec-appendix-a .unnumbered}

This appendix reconciles the existing single-modality derivations (S06, S07) with the evaluated D4 fit and the current implementation in `code/fit_cox_on_yf.R` and its update files (S04). It derives the updates the evaluated algorithm uses, states where the implementation departs from the joint mathematical model, and lists the approximations. Equation numbers continue from the main text.

## A.1 Model and variational family {.unnumbered}

<!-- REVISIT R1 START -->
<!-- REVISIT R2 START -->

The joint model combines the reconstruction @eq-recon with a Cox model for $(t_i, \delta_i)$ whose linear predictor is $\eta_i = \tilde z_i^\top\tilde\beta$, where $\tilde z_i = D^{-1}\bar F^\top y_i$ is the normalized projection of @eq-zf. Priors are $L_{ik} \sim g_{L,k}$ and $F_{jk} \sim g_{F,k}$ (point-exponential) and $\tilde\beta_k \sim g_{\beta,k} = N(0, \sigma_k^2)$. The variational family is fully factorized,
$$
q(L, F, \tilde\beta) = \prod_{i,k} q(L_{ik}) \prod_{j,k} q(F_{jk}) \prod_k q(\tilde\beta_k),
$$
with $\tau$ and the prior parameters treated as point estimates. Write $\bar L_{ik} = E_q L_{ik}$ and $\overline{L^2}_{ik} = E_q L_{ik}^2$, and similarly for $F$ and $\tilde\beta$.

Two features of the predictor matter for every derivation below. First, $\tilde z_i$ is formed from the posterior mean $\bar F$, not from $F$ itself, and $D$ is computed from $\bar F$ at the start of each outer iteration. The projection is therefore a fixed covariate within an iteration: it has no posterior variance in the coefficient update. Second, $L$ does not appear in $\eta$.

<!-- REVISIT R2 END -->
<!-- REVISIT R1 END -->

## A.2 Cox working approximation {.unnumbered}

<!-- REVISIT R1 START -->

Let $\hat\eta$ be the predictor at the start of an iteration, $\hat\theta_i = \exp(\hat\eta_i)$, and $\hat H_0$ the Breslow cumulative baseline hazard with ties sharing a risk-set denominator. The score and the diagonal of the negative Hessian of $\log\mathrm{PL}$ with respect to $\eta_i$ are approximated by
$$
u_i = \delta_i - \hat\theta_i\hat H_0(t_i), \qquad w_i = \hat\theta_i\hat H_0(t_i),
$$ {#eq-a-score}
with $w_i$ floored at $10^{-6}$. A second-order expansion with this diagonal curvature gives
$$
\log\mathrm{PL}(\eta) \approx c - \tfrac12\sum_i w_i (z_i - \eta_i)^2, \qquad z_i = \hat\eta_i + u_i / w_i.
$$ {#eq-a-working}
The exact Hessian of the partial likelihood is not diagonal; dropping its off-diagonal terms is the first approximation. When `strata_id` is supplied, risk sets and $\hat H_0$ are formed within strata; the evaluated fit has no strata.

<!-- REVISIT R1 END -->

## A.3 EBNM handoff {.unnumbered}

Every coordinate update below reduces to the same form. If the expected log objective, as a function of one scalar parameter $\theta$, is $B\theta - \frac12 A\theta^2 + \text{const}$ with $A > 0$, it equals the log-likelihood of a single Gaussian observation
$$
x = B/A, \qquad x \mid \theta \sim N(\theta, s^2), \qquad s = A^{-1/2}.
$$ {#eq-a-ebnm}
The posterior under the prior $g$ is the empirical-Bayes normal-means posterior for $(x, s)$, computed by `ebnm`, which also estimates $g$ by marginal likelihood when $g$ is shared across a vector of observations. The KL term needed for the objective follows from the identity
$$
\mathrm{KL}(q \,\Vert\, g) = E_q\big[\log N(x; \theta, s^2)\big] - \log p(x),
$$ {#eq-a-kl}
where $p(x)$ is the marginal likelihood returned by `ebnm`.

## A.4 Coefficient update {.unnumbered}

<!-- REVISIT R1 START -->
<!-- REVISIT R2 START -->

Isolate factor $k$: $\eta_i = \tilde Z_{ik}\tilde\beta_k + \eta_{i,-k}$, with $\eta_{i,-k} = \sum_{l\ne k}\tilde Z_{il}\bar{\tilde\beta}_l$. Substituting into @eq-a-working and taking the expectation over $q(\tilde\beta_k)$ with $\tilde Z$ fixed, the terms in $\tilde\beta_k$ are
$$
\tilde\beta_k \sum_i w_i \tilde Z_{ik}(z_i - \eta_{i,-k}) - \tfrac12\tilde\beta_k^2\sum_i w_i\tilde Z_{ik}^2 .
$$
The implementation multiplies the survival term by the weight $\alpha$:
$$
A_{\beta,k} = \alpha\sum_i w_i \tilde Z_{ik}^2, \qquad B_{\beta,k} = \alpha\sum_i w_i\tilde Z_{ik}(z_i - \eta_{i,-k}).
$$ {#eq-a-beta}
The pseudo-observation $B/A$ does not depend on $\alpha$; its standard error is inflated by $\alpha^{-1/2}$ ($\sqrt 2$ at the evaluated $\alpha = 0.5$). The prior is normal with variance estimated by `ebnm` from this single pseudo-observation, which gives $\hat\sigma_k^2 = \max(0, x^2 - s^2)$: a coefficient whose pseudo-observation is smaller than its standard error is set exactly to zero. With $\tilde Z$ treated as fixed, @eq-a-beta uses $\tilde Z_{ik}^2$ where the joint model would use $E(\tilde Z_{ik}^2)$; posterior uncertainty in $F$ does not reach the coefficient.

<!-- REVISIT R2 END -->
<!-- REVISIT R1 END -->

## A.5 Activity update {.unnumbered}

<!-- REVISIT R1 START -->

Only the reconstruction term contains $L$. With the factor-$k$ residual $R^{(-k)} = Y - \sum_{l\ne k}\bar L_{\cdot l}\bar F_{\cdot l}^\top$, the expected log-likelihood of @eq-recon contributes, for patient $i$,
$$
L_{ik}\sum_j \tau_j R^{(-k)}_{ij}\bar F_{jk} - \tfrac12 L_{ik}^2\sum_j\tau_j\overline{F^2}_{jk},
$$
so
$$
A_{L,k} = \sum_j \tau_j \overline{F^2}_{jk}, \qquad B_{L,ik} = \sum_j \tau_j R^{(-k)}_{ij}\bar F_{jk},
$$ {#eq-a-L}
with one shared precision $A_{L,k}$ across patients and a point-exponential prior fitted by `ebnm` over the $n$ pseudo-observations. This is the standard empirical-Bayes matrix factorization update; it holds in every configuration of the single-modality model because $\eta$ does not depend on $L$.

<!-- REVISIT R1 END -->

## A.6 Loading update {.unnumbered}

<!-- REVISIT R1 START -->

**Reconstruction contribution.** By the same argument as @eq-a-L with the roles of $L$ and $F$ exchanged,
$$
A^{\mathrm{gen}}_{F,jk} = \tau_j\sum_i\overline{L^2}_{ik}, \qquad B^{\mathrm{gen}}_{F,jk} = \tau_j\sum_i R^{(-k)}_{ij}\bar L_{ik}.
$$ {#eq-a-F-gen}

**Survival contribution in the joint model.** Because $\eta$ depends on $F$, the joint model also has a survival term in the loading update. Treating the normalizing constant $d_k$ as fixed and writing $\tilde Z_{ik} = d_k^{-1}\sum_j y_{ij}F_{jk}$, the terms of @eq-a-working in $F_{jk}$ are, up to factors of $d_k$,
$$
F_{jk}\,E(\tilde\beta_k)\sum_i w_i y_{ij}\big(z_i - \eta_{i,-k}\big) - \tfrac12 F_{jk}^2 E(\tilde\beta_k^2)\sum_i w_i y_{ij}^2 - F_{jk}E(\tilde\beta_k^2)\sum_i w_i y_{ij}\tilde Z^{(-j)}_{ik},
$$
where the last term couples feature $j$ to the other features through the projection excluding $j$. A full treatment would also differentiate $d_k$ with respect to $F_{jk}$.

**Implemented formula.** `update_F_surv_YFB_k()` combines the two sources with weights $1-\alpha_F$ and $\alpha_F$:
$$
A_{F,jk} = (1-\alpha_F)A^{\mathrm{gen}}_{F,jk} + \alpha_F E(\tilde\beta_k^2)\sum_i w_iy_{ij}^2, \quad
B_{F,jk} = (1-\alpha_F)B^{\mathrm{gen}}_{F,jk} + \alpha_F E(\tilde\beta_k)\sum_i w_iy_{ij}(z_i - \eta_{i,-k}).
$$ {#eq-a-F}
This survival branch uses the unnormalized $y_{ij}$, omits the feature-coupling term and the derivative of $d_k$, and updates all features of factor $k$ in one vectorized call. The plain Bayesian posterior corresponds to adding both sources with weight 1, which has the same pseudo-observation as $\alpha_F = 0.5$ and twice its precision (S38). **In the evaluated fit $\alpha_F = 0$**, so @eq-a-F reduces to @eq-a-F-gen and the survival branch is not used. The F update is then the reconstruction update of empirical-Bayes matrix factorization, with the point-exponential prior fitted by `ebnm` over the $p$ pseudo-observations.

<!-- REVISIT R1 END -->

## A.7 Precision update {.unnumbered}

<!-- REVISIT R1 START -->

Maximizing the expected reconstruction log-likelihood over $\tau_j$ gives
$$
\tau_j = \frac{n}{\sum_i E_q\big(y_{ij} - L_i^\top F_j\big)^2}, \qquad E_q\big(y_{ij} - L_i^\top F_j\big)^2 = \big(y_{ij} - \bar L_i^\top\bar F_j\big)^2 + \sum_k\big(\overline{L^2}_{ik}\overline{F^2}_{jk} - \bar L_{ik}^2\bar F_{jk}^2\big),
$$ {#eq-a-tau}
with a floor that bounds $\tau_j$ by $10^8$. There is no prior on $\tau_j$.

<!-- REVISIT R1 END -->

## A.8 Monitoring objective and stopping rule {#sec-appendix-a-objective .unnumbered}

<!-- REVISIT R1 START -->

After each outer iteration the implementation computes
$$
J = (1-\alpha)\,G + \alpha\,p\,S + \sum_k\big(\kappa_{L,k} + \kappa_{F,k} + \kappa_{\beta,k}\big),
$$ {#eq-a-J}
where $G = \sum_j\big[\frac n2\log\tau_j - \frac{\tau_j}{2}\sum_i E_q(y_{ij} - L_i^\top F_j)^2\big]$ is the reconstruction log-likelihood without its constant, $S = \log\mathrm{PL}(\hat\eta) - \frac12\sum_i w_i\mathrm{Var}_q(\eta_i)$ with $\mathrm{Var}_q(\eta_i) = \sum_k\tilde Z_{ik}^2\mathrm{Var}_q(\tilde\beta_k)$, and each $\kappa$ is $-\mathrm{KL}$ computed by @eq-a-kl. The factor $p$ comes from the `per_p` normalization convention, which scales only this monitored quantity. The algorithm stops at the first iteration after the fifth with $|J_t - J_{t-1}|/|J_{t-1}| < 10^{-5}$. Because $J$ weights its components by $1-\alpha$ and $\alpha p$, and because $\log\mathrm{PL}$ is evaluated at the iteration's starting predictor, $J$ is a convergence monitor. It is not the evidence lower bound of the joint model, and the updates are not guaranteed to increase it.

<!-- REVISIT R1 END -->

## A.9 Orientation and prediction {.unnumbered}

<!-- REVISIT R2 START -->

After the loop the implementation checks the training concordance of $\eta$ once and negates $\bar{\tilde\beta}$ if the score is discordant. Before September 4, 2026 this check omitted `reverse = TRUE` in `survival::concordance()`, so it was inverted, and it also replaced $E(\tilde\beta^2)$ by $E(\tilde\beta)^2$ when it negated. The saved D4 fit was produced by that code: its $\eta$ is a good-prognosis score and its stored coefficient variances are zero. It is scored as $\mathrm{risk} = -\eta$ for all held-out cohorts (S01, S49).

For a new patient with data standardized in its own cohort, prediction restricts $\bar F$ to the training genes measured in that cohort but keeps the training normalizing constants $D$, which were computed at the start of the final iteration: $\eta_{\mathrm{new}} = y_{\mathrm{new}}^\top\bar F_{\mathcal{G}}D^{-1}\bar{\tilde\beta}$, where $\mathcal{G}$ is the set of shared genes. Recomputing these projections from the saved fit reproduces the saved held-out scores to within $10^{-8}$ (S49).

<!-- REVISIT R2 END -->

## A.10 Mathematical model versus evaluated algorithm {.unnumbered}

<!-- REVISIT R1 START -->
<!-- REVISIT R2 START -->

| Component | Joint mathematical model | Implementation (`fit_cox_on_yf()`) | Evaluated D4 fit |
|------------|----------------------|----------------------|----------------------|
| Survival term | Exact Cox partial likelihood, expected under $q$ | Diagonal quadratic surrogate @eq-a-working at the iteration's starting $\hat\eta$ | Same; no strata |
| Predictor | $\eta = \tilde z^\top\tilde\beta$ with $\tilde z$ a function of $F$ | $\tilde Z = Y\bar F D^{-1}$ from posterior means, fixed within an iteration | Same |
| Coefficient update | Uses $E(\tilde Z^2)$ including loading uncertainty | Uses $\tilde Z^2$ (plug-in); survival term weighted by $\alpha$ | $\alpha = 0.5$; normal prior with per-factor variance |
| Activity update | Reconstruction only | Reconstruction only | Same |
| Loading update | Reconstruction plus survival with feature coupling and $\partial d_k/\partial F$ | Weighted sum @eq-a-F, survival branch without coupling or normalization derivative | $\alpha_F = 0$: reconstruction only |
| Precision | Maximum likelihood or prior | Maximum likelihood @eq-a-tau | Same |
| Objective | Evidence lower bound | Weighted monitor @eq-a-J | Stopped at iteration 20 |
| Orientation | Not part of the model | One post-fit training check | Pre-September check; risk $= -\eta$ |
| Coefficient uncertainty | Posterior variance of $\tilde\beta$ | $E(\tilde\beta^2)$ retained after the September fix | Stored variances are zero (historical code) |

: Single-modality joint model, implementation, and evaluated fit. Sources: S04, S05, S06, S07, S49, S58. {#tbl-math-vs-impl}

<!-- REVISIT R2 END -->
<!-- REVISIT R1 END -->

The single-modality algorithm therefore performs exact coordinate updates of an empirical-Bayes factorization for $L$, $F$ and $\tau$, interleaved with a plug-in empirical-Bayes update of the Cox coefficients on fixed projections. The derivation of a survival-informed loading update that is stable is part of the continuing work (@sec-continuing).
